OWN QUESTION (both halves settled from the full text). Volume and route: 0.2 ml per weal, injected intradermally through a 25-gauge needle, flexor surface of the forearm, weals on alternate sides of a drawn line, eight weals per forearm - an intradermal weal, not a subcutaneous injection; recorded only here, in the paper card and in D008's reason, per the brief's own-question exception. Endpoint: time to HALF recovery (T50, y=0.5) of sharp pinprick, read off a fitted exponential recovery curve, as the stated measure of duration of action. Full recovery WAS recorded, but not as the endpoint and not per agent: testing ran until four sharp pricks were felt at every weal on the same test or until 240 min, and complete recovery is reported only as a range across all weals of all solutions, 85-240 min. Per-agent half-recovery times from Table II (p. 589, mean +/- SE, min): lignocaine 18.2 +/- 3.8 at the lower strength and 31.4 +/- 4.6 at the higher; bupivacaine 40.5 +/- 6.3 and 76.5 +/- 8.0; etidocaine 17.4 +/- 6.2, 56.9 +/- 10.3 and 91.3 +/- 9.8 across three strengths (concentrations omitted per the brief).

INJECTION PAIN - the point the task flagged. Pain WAS recorded, and the paper did NOT rank the three agents on it: 'During these experiments, stinging was a common experience with all test solutions.' (p. 589). That is the only pain sentence in the paper; no pain scale, no statistics, no ordering. The working hypothesis in my assignment - that this paper is 'the one that is cited' for the etidocaine-worse finding - is WRONG. The cited paper is Howe & Williams 1994, J Dermatol Surg Oncol 20(7):459-64, PMID 8034840, named as such in every citing passage in the record (bupivacaine-wheals, the comparison page, the wheal-literature page and 'What is still unsettled'), and its ordering is verified independently in Europe PMC: 'Lidocaine hurt least and etidocaine hurt most.' Morgan & Russell 1975 is a second, earlier, non-pH-matched intradermal comparison of the same three agents that found no difference, so the record's 'What has no source' sentence is right in substance and attribution but leaves out that the ranking is uncorroborated (finding F001/F006).

RUSSELL' (p. 586), with both authors at Hammersmith Hospital and the Royal Postgraduate Medical School. The Amass BiomedCore record for PMID 1138776 gives exactly two authors, Morgan and W. J. Russell. Title, year, journal, volume, first page, PMID and DOI all match papers_list.csv, so this is the right paper and the three-author form in the assignment is an error, not a different paper. NOT RESOLVED. Geddes 1956 (PMID 13293283) has no abstract anywhere reachable and its full text is subscription-only, so whether it timed an amethocaine/tetracaine analogue in human skin - which would bear on D045 - could not be established; D045 is left as it stands. Sinha 1936 (J Pharmacol Exp Ther 57:199) has no Europe PMC record at all. Howe & Williams 1994's millimetre pain values and injected volume remain paywalled, exactly as the record already says.

PAGES CHECKED AND LEFT WITHOUT A FINDING. mepivacaine-wheals: its six 'half-recovery' passages are all about Fairley & Reynolds 1981; mepivacaine was not tested in 1975, so nothing bears on it. ropivacaine-wheals: its seven etidocaine mentions are animal nerve-injury and fibre-selectivity studies (Kalichman 1988/1989, Gissen 1980); no human intradermal overlap. '5 - Soft ground' and 'What was searched for and does not exist' concern the topical Reference and Guide and contain no mention of etidocaine, injection pain or the weal literature. Product Guide 'Etidocaine' entry and Reference section 4.8 head their entries 'Magnitude UNKNOWN by the topical route - Duration unmeasured - Evidence NONE'; both are explicitly scoped to the topical route in the same sentence and both bodies say no topical study exists, which is right, so neither gets a finding - but it is worth knowing that the record holds no injected-route duration for etidocaine anywhere, and this paper supplies one.

FILTERS AND RULES. No write was stopped by a content filter; everything intended was written. No dose ceiling, maximum dose, overdose or toxicity threshold, antidote passage or preparation/mixing step was copied: the paper's p. 590 passage on etidocaine strength against bupivacaine's systemic toxicity, and its p. 590 remark on a stronger bupivacaine solution reported from clinical practice, were read and deliberately left out of every file. Drug concentrations are replaced by '[dose figure omitted]' throughout; the 0.2 ml weal volume appears only in the paper card and in D008's reason, as what the study did, under the brief's own-question exception. Durations, subject counts and the number of weals are kept as design, n and outcome figures.
